access: Anonymous HTTPS GET/POST to the public ArcGIS REST query endpoint, at most one request per second per host, no token or cookie. Only object-ID, native-ID and county/town scope fields were ever requested; no owner, address, sale, account or taxpayer fields.
helperScripts: tmp/adapter-staging/us-statewide-a/scripts/ (state-cities.py, polite.mjs, meta.mjs, uniqueness.mjs, statewide-repeats.mjs, coverage.mjs, blank-breakdown.mjs, dup-ids.mjs, repeat-geometry.mjs, distinct-area-repeats.mjs, parts-overlap.mjs, verify.mjs, verify-parts.mjs, dense-cell.mjs, descriptors.mjs)

coverage.note: All 88 Ohio counties present. No publisher description on the service.

identity.why: LocalParcelID is the county auditor parcel number (county-scoped). StateParcelID equals 39 + county FIPS + LocalParcelID but every SQL predicate on it fails (HTTP 200 body error 400 "Unable to perform query"), so the adapter could not query it; County~LocalParcelID is the equivalent queryable key. GlobalID is per row and stability across republication is unknown.
identity.queryability: StateParcelID =, IN and LIKE predicates all rejected; LocalParcelID, County and GlobalID predicates work.
identity.exclusion: attributeExclusions LocalParcelID ['', ' '] (excludes null, empty and single-space; SQL Server comparison ignores trailing spaces).

uniqueness.result: County~LocalParcelID is unique per bbox in Columbus/Parma/Cincinnati, but Franklin (13) and Hamilton (67) publish some IDs on several non-overlapping polygons, plus byte-identical stacked copies; hence nativeGeometryMode parts. disjointParts was tried and rejected: stacked identical copies of an already-unioned part trip the overlap check (Hamilton 0940008042100 failed), so plain union is used. Hamilton stacks identical condominium polygons under distinct IDs (31 shared polygons in the Cincinnati bbox).

denseCellTiming: A 0.003 degree Cincinnati cell returned 151 parcels in 18.3 s over 9 requests (each under 2.7 s).
caveats: StateParcelID (39 + county FIPS + LocalParcelID) is published but the service rejects every SQL predicate on it (HTTP 200 error 400), so the equivalent County~LocalParcelID composite is used.

Some counties publish one LocalParcelID on several polygons (13 IDs in Franklin, 67 in Hamilton); all components are fetched and unioned. Byte-identical copies of a component also repeat, so disjointParts is off (with it on, Hamilton 0940008042100 failed); sampled distinct components did not overlap.
Hamilton County stacks byte-identical condominium polygons under distinct LocalParcelIDs (31 shared polygons in one 0.01 degree Cincinnati box).

About 25,000 rows carry no usable LocalParcelID (e.g. 5,664 null in Franklin, 1,709 single-space in Hamilton) and are outside this source; a few counties put free-text notes in LocalParcelID, which are kept verbatim.
metricSrid 32617 suits central/eastern Ohio; cities west of 84 W (e.g. Cincinnati, Dayton) need 32616 when qualified.
